maps.summary: The managed local stack is a set of tested backend pieces with no production caller. Main dispatches only 'hardware.read' and 'runtime.inspect' (src/main/index.ts:221-222). ActivationStore, ManagedOllamaProvider and selectLocal are imported only by tests and the scripts/check-*.ts verifiers. The model.* IPC methods are declared (src/shared/params.ts:121-126), but the engine has no case for them and its default branch throws NOT_IMPLEMENTED (src/engine/application.ts:265). The catalogue is an Ed25519-signed JSON envelope. Its signature covers the domain prefix 'MoonAliza activation set v1\0' plus the payload bytes, and it is checked against an app-supplied trustedKeys map before the payload is parsed (catalogue.ts:24-32). There is no production key, no shipped catalogue, no catalogue producer script and no fetch or update channel in the repository; the docs list 'production trust inputs' as open work (HANDOFF.md:46; docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-27-managed-artifacts.md:20). A catalogue entry carries only identities and links: artifacts {id, role, sha256, sizeBytes, https url, redirectHosts} plus runtimes and configurations that point to a model manifest, model blobs, a lab receipt and an evidence blob (catalogue.ts:10-16). Context size, backend, quantisation, quality and toolsPassed come from the referenced lab-receipt blob (contracts.ts:70-72). Quantisation also comes from the GGUF config blob's file_type (model-store.ts:50,56). No field holds a display name, licence, parameter count or minimum RAM. Activation downloads every artifact in the set (runtime.ts:112-115) and checks each lab receipt: suite moonaliza-coding-v1, quality >= 0.85, tools passed, zero unauthorized effects (runtime.ts:43). It then extracts the Ollama runtime ZIP, copies all model blobs into a private Ollama store named moonaliza/<manifest-sha>:verified (model-store.ts:56), and swaps a single current.json pointer that keeps the previous set (runtime.ts:117-130). Serving is a private Ollama 0.34.4 process started per request. It runs on CPU only (num_gpu 0, zero VRAM is checked), with cloud disabled, on an owned loopback port with socket ownership proof. The scheduler stops the runtime after every inference (scheduler.ts:171-172; managed-provider.ts:11,23-29; managed-ollama.ts:77,99-100). Selection reserves max(2 GiB, 15% of total RAM) (select.ts:15). The user's PC was measured at 8,515,145,728 B total and 1,235,644,416 B available (docs/evidence/model-store-runtime.json), so the reserve is 2 GiB, selectLocal returns 'host-reserve' (select.ts:69) and the probe list is empty (select.ts:56) whatever the model size. Its only GPU, an Intel HD 510, reports availableBytes null because native/hardware.cpp:168 always writes null, so no GPU candidate can ever be eligible (select.ts:32). By the code's design, a newer signed catalogue (higher sequence, in the app version range, not expired, signed by a trusted keyId) can be activated without an app release (runtime.ts:99-105). Today no code obtains or applies one. Key rotation is specified to need an app update (docs/specification/source-plan.md:797).

ArtifactSpecSchema {sha256, sizeBytes <= 1e12, https:443 url with no credentials or fragment, redirectHosts <= 8 exact hostnames} (:10-11). downloadArtifact streams into a content-addressed cache <sha>.blob, rehashes cached copies, resumes only with a strong ETag and exact Content-Range, retries a bounded number of times, rejects off-list redirects (:27) and Retry-After over 30 s (:35), and checks free space (:68,79)

extractRuntimeArchive: bounded, streamed yauzl ZIP extraction with path, link, encryption, duplicate and case checks, CRC and sha256, and an absent destination. Used for the Ollama runtime ZIP (:10-71)

Shared guards: regularFile (no symlink, nlink 1) (:6-10), safeArtifactPath (Windows-safe names) (:12-14), privateDirectory (lstat from the filesystem root) (:16-25), requireSpace with a 256 MiB reserve (:26-30), hashFile, boundedJson, atomicJson, serialized lock

materializeModels and verifyModelStore. Accepts only Ollama manifest v2 with allowed layer media types (model, adapter, projector, prompt, template, system, params, license, messages) (:13-14,44). The config blob must be model_format 'gguf' with an empty remote_host/remote_model (:50). Writes manifests/registry.ollama.ai/moonaliza/<sha>/verified and blobs/sha256-<sha> (:16-17), names the model moonaliza/<manifest-sha>:verified with quantization = config file_type (:56), and verifies the full directory inventory (:83-104). clearModelMetadata removes Ollama's derived metadata/ (:76-81)

ActivationStore. activate() takes an envelope (unknown), runs under withRuntimeStopped, rejects rollback and same-sequence replacement (:99-105), downloads ALL artifacts (:112-115), checks lab receipts and model manifests (proofs :36-51), extracts runtimes and checks them against the signed runtime manifest (:52-78,119-123), materializes ALL configurations (:124), then swaps the current.json pointer {sequence, current, previous} (:130). readActive/readSet re-verify the catalogue at the current time, rehash every cached artifact and the model store, and require receipt quantization == installed quantization (:79-92)

Pure local policy: reserve = max(2 GiB, ceil(15% total RAM)) (:15). labEligible requires runtimeDigest == hardware.runtimeIdentity, a supported backend, enough context, and lab quality >= .85 with tools, zero effects and zero writes after cancellation; GPU requires a known adapter availableBytes > 0 (:26-33). Machine receipt limits: <= 30 days old, load <= 90 s, first token <= 30 s, >= 4 tok/s, requiredRam <= available - reserve, VRAM per adapter with no summing (:37-48). Probe order: installed, then smaller modelBytes, then lab quality; CPU modelBytes must be <= headroom (:55-60). selectLocal returns host-reserve (:69) or ranks within a 0.02 quality band (:81-84). There is no cloud fallback

extensionPoints: Add one local model, catalogue side: append artifacts with role model-manifest, model-blob (one per distinct config and layer digest), lab-receipt and evidence (src/models/catalogue.ts:10, ArtifactSpec at src/models/download.ts:11), and one configurations entry {runtimeId, modelManifestId, modelBlobIds, labReceiptId, evidenceId} (catalogue.ts:16). Raise sequence, keep app.min <= app version < app.maxExclusive, set expiresAt, and sign with the 'MoonAliza activation set v1\0' prefix (catalogue.ts:31). Cross-reference validation is at catalogue.ts:36-40 and receipt and manifest proofs at runtime.ts:40-49.

Pinning a model's identities: follow the pattern in scripts/check-model-store.ts:19-30,46-47 (manifest fetched by tag route with its sha256 and size pinned, blobs by digest route, explicit redirectHosts). The planned producer scripts/fetch-catalogue-locks.mts (source-plan.md:2515) does not exist.

Qualification input (blocks every new model): a LabReceipt JSON (src/shared/contracts.ts:72) bound to the model manifest sha, runtime archive sha, backend, quantization, contextTokens and evidence sha, accepted only if it meets runtime.ts:43. A machine receipt (contracts.ts:74) is needed for selectLocal (select.ts:66-89). The planned runner src/models/qualify.ts and scripts/qualify-model.mts (source-plan.md:2592-2594) are absent.

New per-model metadata (display name, licence, tool-calling flag, minimum RAM): PayloadSchema is .strict() with schemaVersion z.literal(1) (catalogue.ts:11-17), and the artifact and configuration objects are strict. A new field therefore needs a schema change [inferred: older apps would reject a payload carrying it, so this path needs an app release]. A licence can already travel as an Ollama 'application/vnd.ollama.image.license' layer (model-store.ts:14), but nothing reads it.

Trust root: CatalogueTrust.trustedKeys (catalogue.ts:19) reaches ActivationStore through options.trust (runtime.ts:17,24). There is no production construction; it would be added where main builds the store [inferred: near src/main/index.ts, which today wires only hardware.read and runtime.inspect at :221-222].

Catalogue delivery and update: ActivationStore.activate(input: unknown, signal) (runtime.ts:99) is the only ingestion point. No code fetches an envelope (no URL, no IPC). The model.* IPC contracts exist (src/shared/params.ts:121-126) but need engine or main handlers (src/engine/application.ts:265 default NOT_IMPLEMENTED).

Serving: ManagedOllamaProvider takes resolveConfiguration(lease) returning {installation: RuntimeInstallation, configuration: ManagedConfiguration} (managed-provider.ts:41). Its RuntimeInstallation.version (managed-ollama.ts:15) and ManagedConfiguration.outputTokens (managed-provider.ts:10) appear in neither the catalogue runtime entry (catalogue.ts:15) nor the lab receipt (contracts.ts:72), so the resolver must source them elsewhere [inferred gap].

Hardware and ranking input for direction 3: reserve at select.ts:15, probe admission and order at select.ts:55-60, machine-receipt ranking at select.ts:80-86. Main currently probes with runtimeIdentity 'unmanaged;moonaliza-<ver>' (index.ts:221), but labEligible requires runtimeDigest == hardware.runtimeIdentity (select.ts:28), so a resolver must re-probe with the runtime archive sha (model-store-selection.md:25).

GPU placement (none possible today): managed-provider.ts:11 fixes placement to the literal 'cpu' and num_gpu 0 (:23). A GPU candidate needs a non-null adapter availableBytes (select.ts:32), which native/hardware.cpp:168 never produces; the NVML-to-DXGI mapping is unimplemented (hardware.cpp:80-96).

A new runtime version or backend: add a runtimes entry plus runtime and runtime-manifest artifacts (catalogue.ts:15). This requires new lab receipts for every configuration on it (runtime.ts:43 binds receipt.runtimeDigest; source-plan.md:793 'Do not activate a new runtime with stale lab receipts').
invariants: The signature is verified before any payload field is read; tampered bytes, an unknown keyId and a signature without the domain prefix all fail with CATALOGUE_SIGNATURE (src/models/catalogue.ts:25-32; tests/catalogue.test.ts:19-24).
The trust root is application configuration; a document cannot supply its own keys (catalogue.ts:28; tests/catalogue.test.ts:40; docs/specification/managed-artifacts.md:7).

Sequence is monotonic: lower is CATALOGUE_ROLLBACK and same-sequence replacement is refused (catalogue.ts:42; runtime.ts:103-105). Expired, future-dated or out-of-app-range catalogues are refused (catalogue.ts:43-45).

Activation is atomic: a complete set is staged and the single current.json pointer is replaced; failure or cancellation keeps the previous set (runtime.ts:117-134; managed-artifacts.md:11). Activation must hold the runtime-stopped maintenance lease (runtime.ts:100-101).

Model identity is never delegated to mutable 'ollama pull' tags (source-plan.md:2527). The owned transport forbids every management route except version, tags, ps, status and chat (owned-transport.ts:13-14).

No lab receipt means no activation. The receipt must be suite moonaliza-coding-v1, quality >= 0.85, toolsPassed, unauthorizedEffects 0, writesAfterCancellation 0, with matching model, runtime and evidence digests and a supported backend (runtime.ts:43). Receipt quantization must equal the installed file_type (runtime.ts:90).
Only local GGUF is allowed; remote or cloud model configuration is rejected (model-store.ts:44,50). The runtime must report cloud disabled (managed-ollama.ts:77,99-100).

The host-memory reserve max(2 GiB, ceil(15% of total RAM)) must remain free (select.ts:15,41,56,69; source-plan.md:2672). Disk bytes are only a CPU admission filter, never a RAM estimate (select.ts:57; model-store-selection.md:33).

Unknown VRAM stays unknown and multi-GPU free memory is never summed (select.ts:43-46; source-plan.md:772-773). Managed placement is CPU-only until GPU attestation exists (managed-provider.ts:17; managed-provider.md:31).
A local failure never triggers a cloud fallback (select.ts:65; source-plan.md:2610). Cloud models stay behind the project inference policy (plan 2026-10-02-research-jobs.md:408).

Private signing keys never ship and are never committed; rotation and revocation travel only through a trusted app update (source-plan.md:797; HANDOFF.md:146; docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-27-managed-artifacts.md:20). Tests use generated keys and cannot mint real qualification claims.

Downloads use HTTPS on 443 only, with no URL credentials, no cookies, an explicit redirect-host allowlist and exact size plus sha256 before publication (download.ts:10,23,27,96-97). A 256 MiB free-space reserve is kept (artifact-files.ts:26).
The managed runtime is started only from verified installation metadata, never from renderer or model input (managed-ollama.ts:54; managed-provider.md:17).
risks: On the user's PC no managed local model can be offered today, at any size. The retained measurement is total 8,515,145,728 B and available 1,235,644,416 B (docs/evidence/model-store-runtime.json). 15% of total is about 1.19 GiB, so the reserve is 2 GiB and headroom is negative: selectLocal returns 'host-reserve' (select.ts:69) and planProbeCandidates returns [] (select.ts:56). [inferred arithmetic] Even the already-pinned Qwen3 0.6B (522,653,767 B) needs at least about 2.49 GiB available just to be probe-eligible.

The GPU path is closed: the only adapter is an Intel HD 510 with 128 MiB dedicated memory and availableBytes null, which the native probe always reports (native/hardware.cpp:168). Managed placement is the literal 'cpu' (managed-provider.ts:11).

Activation is whole-catalogue, not per-model: activate() downloads every artifact and materializes every configuration in the set (runtime.ts:112-115,124). [inferred] Adding models to one signed set makes every install fetch all of them; 'one-click per model' needs either one set per model (but there is a single current pointer, runtime.ts:130) or an ActivationStore change.

[inferred from code] Expiry and app version can disable an installed set. readSet re-runs verifyCatalogue at the current time (runtime.ts:82 → catalogue.ts:43-45), so after expiresAt, or after an app upgrade past app.maxExclusive, readActive throws CATALOGUE_EXPIRED or CATALOGUE_INCOMPATIBLE. A refresh channel is therefore required, and none exists.

[inferred cost] Every readActive rehashes every cached artifact and the materialized model store (runtime.ts:84-89; model-store.ts:98). Disk use is doubled (the download cache plus a copied store, no hardlinks, conservative retention: model-store-selection.md:7,13; managed-artifacts.md:21). Both grow with each added model.

Nothing produces the inputs a new model needs: no lab-qualification runner, no machine-probe runner, no catalogue producer and no production signing key. qualify.ts, qualify-model.mts and fetch-catalogue-locks.mts are absent, and the docs record 'production trust inputs' as open (HANDOFF.md:46).

Nothing is wired end to end: ActivationStore, ManagedOllamaProvider and selectLocal have no src caller, and model.* IPC falls through to NOT_IMPLEMENTED (src/engine/application.ts:265). The setup UI says managed installation is 'still in development' (LocalModelPanel.tsx:48).

The catalogue runtime entry has no version, yet the runtime start requires /api/version == installation.version (catalogue.ts:15 vs managed-ollama.ts:15,92). outputTokens is in neither the catalogue nor the receipt (managed-provider.ts:10). Main's hardware probe identity 'unmanaged;...' (index.ts:221) can never satisfy select.ts:28.

[inferred] Latency limits for CPU inference. The runtime is cold-started for every request because the scheduler stops it after each inference (scheduler.ts:171-172). Limits are a 300 s lease and process lifetime (managed-provider.ts:50; managed-ollama.ts:82), 120 s per HTTP exchange and a 4 MiB buffered response (owned-transport.ts:19,50), and machine receipts require load <= 90 s, first token <= 30 s and >= 4 tok/s (select.ts:40). Larger models on a weak CPU may never qualify.

Upstream fragility, fail-closed. The registry served the manifest only by tag (a 404 on the digest route), and blobs redirect to one specific R2 hostname (check-model-store.ts:29-30,46; model-store-selection.md:41). A tag republish or CDN host change breaks the catalogue: digest mismatch, or ARTIFACT_REDIRECT (download.ts:27).

Format lock-in: only Ollama manifest v2 with the listed media types and GGUF config are accepted (model-store.ts:13-14,44,50), and the runtime is pinned to the Ollama 0.34.4 windows-amd64 ZIP (check-runtime-artifacts.ts:17-18). Models needing a newer runtime require a runtime update and re-qualification of every model.

Test environment: the baseline Linux gate has 74 known failing tests (docs/orchestration/2026-10-05-more-models/RUN.md:35). The managed-ollama, owned-transport and hardware tests and the real verifiers need the Windows native helper, and check-*.ts throw unless win32/x64 (check-model-store.ts:32).

maps.summary:
ProfileKindSchema declares four kinds (src/shared/contracts.ts:24), but only two run. complete() throws NOT_IMPLEMENTED for every kind except 'openai-compatible' and 'ollama' (src/main/inference.ts:142-143). The renderer's Provider select offers only "Ollama (local)" and "OpenAI-compatible API" (src/renderer/App.tsx:266), and docs/specification/implementation-sources.md:12 says "Responses and Anthropic adapters remain separate implementation work". So the plan's line that Moonzila "already reaches many models through profiles (ollama, openai-compatible, openai-responses, anthropic)" (docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-02-research-jobs.md:401) overstates what works: 'openai-responses' and 'anthropic' are names in the enum with no adapter behind them, no UI and no tests of their own. The 'anthropic' string appears in tests only as a wire-state mismatch value (tests/contracts.test.ts:130), and 'openai-responses' appears in no test.

The one adapter is a single function, complete(), that switches on a boolean `local = kind === 'ollama'` (inference.ts:147). That flag picks the message encoding (:47-73), the tool-call parser (:75-85), the stream reader and accumulator (:129-134), the route (/api/chat or /chat/completions, :157), the request body (:153-155), the usage mapping (:163-164) and the terminal mapping (:167-181).

Streaming happens only at the transport: SSE and NDJSON are folded back into one body (provider-stream.ts:42-60, 71-175). Today the user picks the model for every run; nothing chooses it automatically. The composer has a "Model profile" dropdown (src/renderer/App.tsx:236). It defaults to the first profile that profile.list returns (App.tsx:72, App.tsx:79), and the store sorts profiles alphabetically by name (src/engine/store.ts:169). run.start requires an explicit profileId (src/shared/params.ts:108), and the engine binds the run to that profile revision (src/engine/application.ts:229-235). The only rule applied to the choice is locality. assertConversationPolicy refuses an external profile when the session or the project is local-only (src/engine/policy.ts:68-79, called at application.ts:230 and again on every inference at src/main/index.ts:90), and the renderer disables Send rather than switching profile (App.tsx:62, App.tsx:236). The research-review chooser takes the first profile the policy allows (src/renderer/ResearchPanel.tsx:184, ResearchPanel.tsx:192). Locality is derived from whether the endpoint host is loopback (src/main/inference.ts:18-20). Only the openai-compatible and ollama kinds can run: anthropic and openai-responses throw NOT_IMPLEMENTED (inference.ts:143), and the profile form offers only those two (App.tsx:266).

src/models/select.ts is a pure, local-only policy. It gates candidates on a moonaliza-coding-v1 lab receipt with quality >= 0.85, machine receipts at most 30 days old, RAM headroom above max(2 GiB, 15% of RAM), and known free VRAM per adapter (select.ts:15, select.ts:26-48). Among the candidates that pass, it ranks within 0.02 of the best quality: installed first, then quality, then first-token time, throughput and load time (select.ts:80-86). It has no production caller: only tests/selection.test.ts:3 imports it. The model.* IPC methods (params.ts:121-125) have no handler [inferred from grep: no case for them in engine or main, so they reach NOT_IMPLEMENTED at application.ts:265 or src/main/index.ts:298].

No profile or catalogue entry carries a price, quality score, capability flag or task tag (contracts.ts:26, src/models/catalogue.ts:11-17). The only signal per task is the run mode (run.start accepts ask, plan and build, application.ts:232). The only cost-related runtime data is token usage per step (usage.updated, application.ts:363).

The 2026-10-02 research says in its BRIEF that it passed its gate (BRIEF.md:11). All 20 evidence rows were retrieved on 2026-10-02 (EVIDENCE.md:11-30), which makes them 3 days old today. No code relates this floor to a configuration's contextTokens; selectLocal's minimumContextTokens defaults to 512 (select.ts:11). Small-context local configurations, the only kind that might fit a small RAM budget, may hit CONTEXT_LIMIT on every step. [inferred]

Tools are offered regardless of model capability. Every project run sends READ/GIT tools, and in build mode WRITE/COMMAND tools too (application.ts:339-341). Neither ProfileSchema (contracts.ts:26) nor the catalogue (catalogue.ts:16) has a tools-capable flag. Thinking and reasoning handling. complete() sends no thinking control for Ollama (inference.ts:153-155; grep finds no 'think'), and OllamaAccumulator parses `thinking` but discards it (provider-stream.ts:63, :82). All three small families in the corpus are tagged 'thinking' (raw library capture :62 qwen3, :83 gemma4, :104 qwen3.5), including the only pinned model, qwen3:0.6b (scripts/check-model-store.ts:19-27). profile.test caps output at 32 tokens and requires outcome 'complete' (index.ts:276, :280). [inferred] Reasoning that consumes the output budget becomes 'incomplete', then PROVIDER_ERROR, then INTERNAL_ERROR.

Usage and cost accounting contract. TokenUsageSchema has only inputTokens and outputTokens (shared/context.ts:4), with no cached-input or reasoning counts, although vendors price cache hits separately (DeepSeek capture :39-40). usage.updated is per step (application.ts:363), and session.read returns only the latest usage event (application.ts:148), so per-run spend needs summation that does not exist. diagnostics.export is declared (params.ts:153) but unhandled (index.ts:298). There is no telemetry anywhere in src (grep), so no observed-quality data exists to feed ranking.

Settings and migrations. SettingsSchema is strict (params.ts:74), and the engine parses stored settings merged over defaults (application.ts:158). [inferred] A new default-profile or budget field written by a newer app makes an older app's strict parse fail after a downgrade. SCHEMA_VERSION is 4 (migrations.ts:3), but the upgrade fixtures stop at tests/fixtures/schema-v3.sql. Profile price or quality columns need a v5 migration plus a v4 fixture, and putProfile's immutability comparison iterates profileColumns (store.ts:159-160).

Run budgets vs cold-start local inference. Default settings are modelStepBudget 24 and runDurationMinutes 15 (application.ts:158; deadline at :329-331), and the scheduler stops the managed runtime after every inference lease (scheduler.ts:171-172). [inferred] A CPU-only managed model on weak hardware may hit BUDGET_EXCEEDED long before 24 steps, because each step pays a cold load.

E2E coverage for a new external kind. The only e2e provider fake is a loopback /api/chat (e2e/workbench.spec.ts:14). A non-loopback endpoint must be https (inference.ts:19), and a loopback fake is classified 'local', so cloud-policy behaviour for a new external kind needs an https fake with test-time TLS, following tests/fixtures/github-tls.ts. CI (.github/workflows/windows.yml:18-51) never runs scripts/check-model-store.ts or scripts/check-runtime-artifacts.ts, so the real managed path is never exercised in CI.

Non-streaming fallback strictness. When an OpenAI-compatible server answers without text/event-stream, the body is parsed with ChatSchema (inference.ts:130, :40), and tool calls must match OpenAICalls, which is .strict() and requires a string id and type 'function' (inference.ts:43). The streaming accumulator passes `type` through unchanged (provider-stream.ts:172). [inferred] A compatible vendor or router that omits `type` or `id` on tool calls, or adds fields to them, fails as PROVIDER_INVALID_RESPONSE, so the 'reach more models through openai-compatible' path depends on per-vendor wire details.
